messages.subject: Changing Colors
parts:
Hi Folks,

I am messing around with some ggplot code derived from (http://gastonsanchez.com/blog/how-to/2012/10/13/MCA-in-R.html) to work on my own MCA work and I can't figure out how to get the geom_text code to create a gray scale for the categorical variables and the legend. I would love to keep the color, but I can't. 


Here is the code


# plot of variable categories
ggplot(data=mca1_vars_df, 
       aes(x = Dim.1, y = Dim.2, label = rownames(mca1_vars_df))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "gray70") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "gray70") +
  geom_text(aes(colour=Variable)) +                              ************Here is the suspect
  ggtitle("MCA plot of variables using R package FactoMineR")


Any ideas would be awesome.  Also, my apologies in advance for a question that should be easy to figure out, but I've spent over an hour already so I defer to the collective expertise.

Cheers,

Joshua

messages.subject: Re: Changing Colors
parts:
Here's a reproducible (hint!) example:

# load data tea
data(tea)

# select these columns
newtea = tea[, c("Tea", "How", "how", "sugar", "where", "always")]
cats = apply(newtea, 2, function(x) nlevels(as.factor(x)))
mca1 = MCA(newtea, graph = FALSE)

# data frame with variable and observation coordinates
mca1_vars_df = data.frame(mca1$var$coord, Variable = rep(names(cats), cats))
mca1_obs_df = data.frame(mca1$ind$coord)

p <- # ...your ggplot code above
p + scale_color_grey()

HTH,
Ben
